# dsh-mise
Toolchain manager for DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`), backed by mise. One settings page shows what is inst
alled and what is available, and installs, pins, uninstalls and prunes by directory (`.mise.toml`-dr
iven). Nine agent tools expose the same surface to the model, so an agent can see the machine, pick
a version, install it, pin it and clean up afterwards without guessing.
English | 中文
- **Host half** (`src/index.ts` + `src/mise.ts`, built to `dist/`): every `mise` invocation, JSON pa

rsing, the write gate, and a set of endpoints on the plugin's own `/mise` RPC channel.
- **Client ha
lf** (`src/client.ts`, built to `dist/client.js`): a `settings.section` page (order 48) that talks o
nly to that channel — it serves no HTTP route of its own and never touches a binary.
No `@deepseek-ai/*` package is imported at runtime: the host half is plain ESM, the browser half is
one self-contained bundle whose React comes from the harness module table.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Requires `dsh` >= 0.2.0-rc.2 and a `mise` binary on the host (or `miseBin` pointing at one). The bui
ld output in `dist/` is committed, so a source install needs no build step; `mise` itself is not bun
dled — install it from mise.jdx.dev first.
## What the page shows
| Capability | Where |
| One table: the active version, how many versions are installed, what PATH resolves to | Settings →

mise |
| Tools the image ships that mise does not manage | one folded row under the table (`System-

provided · N`), read-only, collapsed by default |
| Manage a tool's versions | the `▸` in front of t
he tool name opens a version sub-table: version, status, install path, and the per-version actions (

use / uninstall, two-step confirm) |
| Newer version available | a dashed `↑1.8.2` marker after the
**active** version only, fed by `mise outdated --inactive --bump --json`; comparisons are mise's own

, never re-implemented |
| Requested by `.mise.toml` but not installed | `not installed` in the curr
ent column, with `install x.y.z` in the sub-table and a table-wide "install everything the config as

ks for" |
| Search | one box: a tool name lists versions, `tool@prefix` (`pnpm@12`) narrows to that

prefix, anything else falls back to a mise registry search |
| Live install output | the panel polls
the running write command every 0.7 s and renders mise's own lines with `\r` redraws collapsed in p
unning write command every 0.7 s and renders mise's own lines with `\r` redraws collapsed in place |
## The nine tools
| Tool | What it does |
| `mise_status` | mise version/path, target directory, config files on the directory chain, active v

ersions, missing versions, and whether CLI activation is on |
| `mise_versions` | installed / active

/ latest / remote versions for a tool, or a registry search for a query |
| `mise_system` | read-on
ly PATH scan of 18 common dev commands: the hit path and version, whether mise also manages that too

l, and the image-provided copy after skipping mise's shims |
| `mise_install` | install `tool@versio

n`; `background: true` returns a task id immediately |
| `mise_use` | write into the project `mise.t

oml` or the global config (installs first if missing) |
| `mise_prune` | remove versions no config r

eferences; `dryRun: true` by default |
| `mise_uninstall` | remove one installed version, plus the c

onfig request that points at it |
| `mise_activate` | switch PATH activation on/off for this host pr

ocess |
| `mise_progress` | read the live progress of one write command (what is running, for how lo
ng, recent lines, whether it finished) |
Writes are recorded as tasks because tool calls are request/response: the panel polls the running on
e, an agent starts with `background: true` and polls `mise_progress`. A large toolchain download the
refore does not pin a single call for fifteen minutes.
## Configuration
Set in the plugin row (or the settings form):
| Field | Default | Meaning |
| `miseBin` | `''` | empty probes PATH, `~/.local/bin/mise`, `/usr/local/bin/mise`, `/opt/homebrew/b

in/mise`, `~/.local/share/mise/bin/mise` |
| `cwd` | `''` | default directory for the panel and the

tools; empty = the host process cwd |
| `env` | `{}` | extra environment for every `mise` child proc

ess |
| `timeoutMs` | `20000` | timeout for read commands (`ls` / `ls-remote` / `registry`) |
| `lon

gTimeoutMs` | `900000` | timeout for `install` / `use` / `prune` |
| `writeMode` | `auto` | `readonl
y` refuses every write; `ask` routes agent writes through DSH's approval seam (and denies when no ap

prover exists); `auto` runs them |
| `remoteLimit` | `30` | remote versions returned per call |
| `r

egistryLimit` | `40` | registry search hits |
| `activate` | `true` | prepend mise's `shims` directo
ry to the host PATH on load, so tool commands work in any shell the host spawns |
## Write boundaries
- Only mise's own install directory and config files are touched; `prune` always runs with `--tools`

, so mise's config-tracking table is left alone.
- Uninstall takes an explicit `tool@version` and is
two steps: `mise uninstall` removes the files, then `mise unuse --path <source.path> --no-prune` re

moves the request that pointed at it — otherwise the row would linger as "not installed".
- A reques
t that was never installed (or is left over from an earlier uninstall) gets its own "remove from con

fig" action, a bare `mise unuse` at the same explicit path.
- A real prune always runs the dry run f

irst; the returned `removed` list is that preview, not a guess.
- Panel buttons are user clicks and

skip approval; agent write tools follow `writeMode`.
- `MISE_AUTO_INSTALL` is not set: installs happ
en only when asked for.
## Activation and persistence
On load the plugin puts `<data dir>/shims` at the front of the host process PATH — the effect of `mi
se activate`, without editing shell config. It applies to that process and the shells it spawns; a t
erminal outside the host is untouched. Managed versions win where a config pins one, and shims fall
back to the system copy otherwise, so a command never disappears.
